title: Saving an edited recording puts the finished video in history, ready to paste
goal: Record, make a few edits, press Save and close: the finished video is in history straight away as a real MP4, so copying or dragging its tile into Teams or Slack gives the edited video, not the raw recording. The edit itself stays re-openable, and the original recording is never lost.
notes:
User's words: "one very key thing. When I open a video, make some edits, save, and close, I really wanted to have it save a copy and put it in history. However, I think i need to export it to get an mp4 that can be embedded in another app. ... i want to be able to record a video, make some edits and save and use it in teams really fast. ... if that is always slow, then I guess just having the exported file in history is good".

From code reading (not run): Next opens recordings as an EditorState timeline document (NextExperience.swift:29-30). Command-S -> EditorState.saveDocument (EditorState.swift:3198-3222) -> saveDocumentAs (:3227-3242) writes a .photonz package referencing the recording (ProjectMedia.table :3244-3262), never rewrites the mp4 (EditorState+RevertRecording.swift:7-12), no CaptureStore call. Export: EditorState+VideoExport.swift:94-180, 318-367, no history entry; verbatim copy only for an untouched whole recording (:338-346), any edit is a full re-encode via DocumentFrames + DocumentMovieWriter (:348-366). Copy Video already renders edits to $TMPDIR/PhotonzClipboard/<name>.mp4 and pastes it (EditorState+VideoExport.swift:255-301, EditorCommands.swift:438-446); reuse that writer. History tile Copy/drag give the stored raw mp4 (AppCoordinator.swift:423-455, CaptureThumbnailView.swift:67, HistoryOverlay.swift:643-650). Save to Capture History (AppCoordinator.swift:888-910) only stores a flattened PNG. Measured export speed: queue/audits/2026-09-27-fast-video-export.json, 5 min Retina at 1080p in 72-83 s (0.23-0.26x running time). Companion task filed the same day: 'Cutting a recording and exporting it copies the pieces instead of re-encoding' makes the common cut-only case near instant.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: record, cut a piece out and add a zoom, Command-S, close. Record in the audit what history shows and what Copy on the tile pastes into a text editor/Finder (expected today: the raw recording; Save writes only a .photonz project)

Command-S on an edited recording keeps the editable project AND writes the edited MP4 in the background (High quality, the recording's own size, matching the Export sheet's MP4); its history tile shows the edited version with a small mark that it was edited, and the raw recording stays available (as its own entry or behind the edited one, the audit says which and why, using IA rules)
While the MP4 is being written the tile shows progress, the window can be closed at once, and quitting mid-write finishes or resumes it rather than losing it

Copy, drag-out and the toast's Copy on that tile give the edited MP4 file, so pasting into Teams or Slack attaches the edited video; MEASURED: time from Save to a pasteable file for a 30 s and a 3 min recording, written in the audit
Opening the tile opens the editable project, not the flattened MP4, so editing again and saving again replaces the edited MP4 in place (one tile, not a new one per save)
An untouched recording still saves nothing new and its tile is unchanged
Save to Capture History on a video no longer puts a single still frame into history; it does the same as above or is hidden for video
Export keeps working and, if the user exports instead, the exported file can also be the tile's file; say in the audit how the two relate
A walk at Next defaults records (or opens the sample recording), edits, saves, closes, and checks the history tile's file is an MP4 whose length matches the edit
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
